conclusion: Carries one copy of the SIRT6 rs117385980 T allele. In two small studies the T allele was less common among the longest-lived participants: long-lived healthy Finnish men, and Iranian adults aged 80 to 90 in whom it was not seen at all. Neither result reached statistical significance (p = 0.074 and p = 0.073), the Iranian cohort found the same allele slightly more common among robust than among frail participants, and its authors described the effect as diverse. Treat this as a weak and unconfirmed direction, not an established effect on lifespan.

Two copies of the reference C allele at SIRT6 rs117385980. The minor T allele that the longevity studies report is absent. This is the common genotype in every population reported by the source papers, and the trend those papers describe in its favour was not statistically significant, so no lifespan advantage is asserted for it here: the weight is an explicit zero rather than a blank. A no-call at this position is not this result and must not be reported as one.

Two copies of the SIRT6 rs117385980 T allele. Neither source study observed this genotype in any participant: both cohorts carried the T allele only in heterozygous form, and population databases record it as rare. Nothing in this module's evidence base speaks to it, so no direction, no significance and no weight are asserted. Any inference from the heterozygous finding to this genotype would be the reader's own, not the cited studies'.
